Subject: Post-call recap: Evaluation on-ramp — perf & acceptance checklist

Evan / team,

Thanks for taking the time earlier — quick recap and a proposed list of acceptance metrics so we can spin up the comparison tests (Redwood hosted/dedicated/private) vs your current vLLM/TGI stack. I tried to capture the pain + goals you called out and a pragmatic set of asks for the bake-onboard:

1) Pain points you shared
- Cost variability: token spend spiking during peak inference windows and unclear per-request unit economics.
- Latency outliers: p99 spikes during multi-user bursts (affects UX for synchronous flows).
- Cold-start and KV-cache warm-up: some prompts require long context/history which currently causes slow first-token times.
- Ops burden of tuning vLLM/TGI across many model variants and maintaining stable autoscaling.

2) Current stack (as discussed)
- Model hosting: self-hosted TGI on GKE (NVIDIA A100s) running vLLM for optimization.
- Inference path: grpc fronting -> request router -> model pods; custom batching layer.
- Observability: Prometheus + internal dashboards; limited token-level cost breakdown.

3) High-level goals for the evaluation
- Preserve or improve generation quality on your internal NLU tests (no more than 2% delta on task F1).
- Reduce p50 latency and tighten p99 under burst (target: p50 <= 120ms, p99 <= 900ms on typical interactive prompts).
- Achieve predictable unit cost with a target blended cost reduction (relative) of 20% at projected monthly volume.
- Demonstrate stable throughput for sustained workload windows (target: 2k concurrent inference sessions with average 256-token sequences).

4) Acceptance/benchmark criteria (what we will measure for the bake-off)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 across warm and cold cache scenarios (end-to-end).
- Throughput: sustained token/sec and QPS under realistic batching policies (batch sizes 1, 8, 16).
- Quality: task F1 on your labeled eval set; hallucination rate on gold QA set (<3% required).
- Cost: tokens-per-dollar for both generation and embeddings (1M-token normalized baseline).
- Reliability: error rate, repro-ing of deterministic prompts, and failover behavior under node loss.
- Ops: time-to-recover from instance restarts, and visibility (token-level traces + audit logs).

5) Specific benchmark asks (what we need from you)
- A 1k-2k sample eval set (we agreed a small sample first) — you mentioned you could share a subset today.
- Target workload profile (1-minute QPS distribution for peak and off-peak).
- Any blocked tokens/resource limits we should respect for your environment (PCI/HIPAA sensitive routes).

6) Redwood comparison matrix items we will produce
- Hosted API (Redwood): latency/throughput/cost and streaming behavior.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): expected throughput per pool shape + autoscale behavior.
- Private (VPC): same workload run inside your GCP region (if you want) or our on-prem package.
- Baselines: TGI self-host + vLLM optimizations (what you are running today) + 1 public cloud-managed endpoint (we can include AWS Bedrock / Azure OpenAI equivalents on request).

7) Next steps / timeline
- You: share the sample eval dataset and peak workload profile (Evan) — ETA: 48 hours.
- Redwood: deliver runner scripts and redwood_eval_matrix_v1.xlsx; estimate for hosted vs dedicated cost and a proposed test schedule — ETA: 48 business hours after dataset.
- Joint: a short triage call once we have data to confirm any additional telemetry we need.

Attachments: redwood_eval_matrix_v1.xlsx (evaluation matrix & measurement plan).

If that captures things correctly, I’ll queue Marcus and Dylan to begin the test harness and cost estimates. Happy to tighten any of the acceptance bullets if you have stronger constraints.

Best,
